preview: Shivani Pawar shares her on-campus internship interview experience for the Enterprise Engineering Track at Morgan Stanley, detailing the AMCAT round and two subsequent interviews.
content:
INTERNSHIP INTERVIEW
Morgan Stanley (2 Month Internship) On-Campus
(Enterprise Engineering Track)
SHIVANI PAWAR - T.Y.B.Tech C.S. 2022
I. Coding Round (for TY CS ,IT, EXTC, Electronics) conducted on
AMCAT
1. Aptitude (10 question and 20min)
It had aptitude questions. This section can be done use some simple
mathematical formulae.They can be found here
https://www.indiastudychannel.com/resources/78963-List-of-Formulas-usef
ul-for-solving-aptitude-questions.aspx
2. Code Debugging 7 ques (20mins)
(Some easy codes like find max product of 3 numbers, find median, find
the smallest distance, area of triangle, loops)
3. Coding (3 questions 1 hour)
I don’t remember the questions, but what I have noticed is, Morgan Stanley
mostly asks questions on backtracking, simple dp problems and hashmap,
which can be done from GFG.
I had solved ⅔ questions completely.
Out of all 11 were selected for the next round (Interview)
II. Interview 1: Technical Round (1-hour)
→ Tell me about yourself (I had prepared this, so I just said that.)
→ Then she asked me to code a question :
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/largest-subarray-with-equal-number-of-0s-and-1s/
I first explained the brute force approach with the cumulative sum array. She
asked me to code it, which I did. She then asked me to optimize it. I tried to , but
after around 5mins because of time constraints we had to move on.
→  What is a deadlock? What are the conditions for a deadlock?
→ What is a semaphore? What is mutex?
→ Explain paging.
→ What is scaling ? I explained horizontal and vertical scaling.
→ What is a Load Balancer?
→ What are the algorithms used in a load balancer it? (I told her I did not know
this)
→ She gave me a scenario (don’t exactly remember it ), in which I was asked
how can I make the data reach faster to the users?
I first suggested caches. I gave an example of Redis. I also mentioned CDNs.
She was not satisfied. Then I suggested using an Asynchronous queue. She
asked for an example. I named Kafka and RabbitMQ. She was happy with my
answer.
(there were some more questions , but I don’t quite remember them).
Out of 11 only 4 were shortlisted
III. Interview 2: Professional Fitness Round (1 hour)
In my previous interview experiences, I made a lot of mistakes in this round. So,
for this interview, I had prepared and practised some common HR questions with
a friend.
→ Tell me about yourself (I had prepared this, so I just said that.)
→ He asked me a few questions on the things I mentioned in ‘tell me about
yourself’
→ Asked me to explain some of my projects (had already prepared this)
→ Asked me to explain how we came up the ideas for those projects
→ whether I had any conflict in some group activity. (I had prepared this answer
as well )
→ whether I had to adjust for some person in any group activity
→ he asked what I do in my free time (he seemed very happy with my answers)
This took only 30 mins, then
→ he asked if I had any questions, I asked a few, and then for the rest of the
interview, he was talking about his experience.
They gave their results after two weeks.
3/4 were selected for the internship
What I have learned from my experience/ some tips:
1. Firstly, about the EE track in Morgan Stanley, the interviews are not very
different from the AppDev track. Expect the same kind of difficulty in
questions. It is just better to know some system design terms like scaling,
load balancers, sharding etc. for this track.
You can also prepare from Gaurav Sen’s or Narendra’s system design
playlists on Youtube.
2. For coding questions, stick to just gfg or leetcode.
In an interview, when asked to code a question, start with the brute force
approach and after that you can optimize it if asked.
While writing the code , continuously communicate with the interviewer.
Sometimes the interviewers don’t expect you to come up with a solution at
all, they just want to see your approach, your attitude towards a problem.
3. For core CS subjects , OS, DBMS. I have found this to be enough
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/last-minute-notes-operating-systems/
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/last-minute-notes-dbms/
4. It is better to be prepared for questions on your projects and questions on
the tech stack you used for your projects.
5. It is better to prepare answers for some common HR questions and
practise them in front of a mirror or with a friend.
6. They don’t expect you to know everything, so don’t try to do everything.
Just be confident in whatever projects and preparation you have done.
7. Lastly, don’t take rejections personally. Everyone makes mistakes. Other
than that, companies reject candidates based on a lot of other reasons
which have nothing to do with the candidate.
The process might seem very difficult after some rejections, but you just
have to keep trying your best, learn from every interview you give and
improve yourself and you will definitely crack it!
All the best! :)
